S1.hook: Tested on the faces walking out.
S1.dek: The pedestrian exit lane at the Progreso International Bridge in Hidalgo County. Over 1.1 million pedestrians a year walk out of the United States here.

S2.dek: Cameras went up on poles at different heights, so people of different statures would land in frame. Some of the testing ran after dark on lighting the partners brought.

S3.hook: Six were shown. Three came south.
S3.dek: Six companies were demonstrated at the Maryland Test Facility. Three solutions were carried forward for data collection at the bridge.

S4.dek: A replica of the pedestrian exit environment went up at the Maryland Test Facility first, so the vendors could install and assess their prototypes before taking them to the crossing.

S5.dek: Artificial intelligence built a three dimensional model of the capture zone, watched pedestrian movement, and judged whether a face was good enough to match. The account gives no rate for how often it was right.

S6.hook: One lane was provided for saying no.
S6.dek: Signs in English and Spanish told pedestrians that United States citizens could opt out. An opt-out lane was provided. The mandate the test serves applies to travelers who are not citizens.

S7.hook: The way in is counted every month.
S7.dek: 101,306 pedestrians entered the United States here in May 2026, the month the partners were at the bridge. No comparable data is collected on the way out.

S8.hook: Cut for eight. Shipped with three.
S8.dek: The account carries three verdicts and five measurements a reader would need. Nothing was removed. None of the five was ever stated.

S9.hook: No room. No window. No date.
S9.dek: This test opens no comment period and no hearing. The nearest dated public room in this record is a different program. Dallas takes a briefing on its police department's Flock plate readers on September 8th, 2026.
